text:
anya: Heads up — eu-west-1 GPU fleet is degraded since 2026-03-18T09:05Z. ~52% allocation failures; queue depth spiking. I attempted DNS failover to us-east by shifting Route53 weights but some customer traffic is still hitting eu-west.

infra-bot: [09:07Z] alert: gpu-pool-eu-west allocation_failure_rate=0.52, avg_alloc_latency=4.1s, pool_available=8/16

mike: Did we pre-lower TTL before changing weights?

anya: We were at 300s. I changed the public record TTL to 60s at 09:10Z but many resolvers still return eu-west IPs.

jen: Lowering TTL after a long TTL rarely helps immediately — caches only drop when their original TTL expires. Some ISP recursive resolvers enforce a minimum TTL (300s or more), plus registry/registrar glue can be sticky.

carla: Can you paste dig from multiple resolvers? need to see divergence.

anya: dig +short A model-api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8 -> 34.201.12.45 (us-east)
8.8.4.4 -> 34.201.12.45
1.1.1.1 -> 52.18.7.33 (eu-west)
9.9.9.9 -> 52.18.7.33

mike: So it's resolver-split. 8.8.8.8 picked up weight change quickly; Cloudflare/quad9 still serving old cache.

jen: Two practical ways: 1) use a new hostname (failover-host) and switch CNAMEs so clients resolve a fresh name, bypassing existing cache; or 2) do application-level fallback — have SDK try alternate endpoint on connection failure. 1 is faster if clients don't have pinned hostnames.

carla: We can't update client SDK mid-flight for all customers. New hostname approach could work for web/HTTP clients but not for long-lived TCP connections. Also watch for CNAME flattening at the apex.

anya: For immediate mitigation I'm starting a weighted-change script to push 95% -> us-east and 5% -> eu-west to avoid flip flop. Running: 
```
./ops/traffic-shift.sh --provider route53 --record model-api.redwood.example.com --weight-target 95 --region us-east-1
```

deploy-bot: [09:15Z] runbook: traffic-shift.sh executed by anya — new weights applied (us-east:95, eu-west:5)

mike: Also, spin up extra dedicated GPU capacity in us-east. Triggering autoscale with larger instance types now. Cost impact: estimated +35% for next 6 hours. Approving since latency SLOs are impacted.

anya: K8s rollout for larger pools started: `kubectl -n infra apply -f gpu-pool-us-east-scale.yaml`

infra-bot: [09:20Z] event: k8s rollout gpu-pool-us-east replicas=12->20, image=runtime-v2.3.1

jen: Note for post-incident: lowering TTL pre-emptively for critical hostnames before maintenance is the only reliable way to reduce propagation time. We should keep critical hostnames at <=60s TTL during business hours.

carla: Another option: use a provider that supports on-the-fly failover with Anycast + health checks (makes propagation near-instant from edge), or use HTTP-level steering via CDN. Both are product changes.

mike: Short-term: continue weight shift + capacity spin up. Medium-term: add app-level multi-region fallback and a hot standby hostname that we can point to with clients that support failover.

anya: Observed weirdness: some customers resolve eu-west for 20+ minutes after weight change. Likely negative caching or intermediate resolver misbehavior. Documenting ASNs where this happens: AS12345, AS54321.

jen: Add resolver-health metric to console: percent of successful lookups returning us-east vs eu-west by ASN. That will help detect split-resolution during incidents. Owner: carla.

carla: I'll own the metric and add an alert for >10% split at 5m intervals.

mike: For partial mitigation we can also route non-critical/low-SLA traffic to quantized model variants hosted in other regions — cheaper to serve and reduces GPU pressure. Plan that for next week.

anya: Action items: 1) Complete traffic shift to us-east until eu-west is healthy (anya) 2) Ramp us-east capacity (mike) 3) Add split-resolution metrics and alerts (carla) 4) Update runbook: pre-lower TTLs ahead of planned ops + registrar notes (jen). I'll update the incident doc.

jen: One more note — some registrars will ignore TTLs below a provider-specific floor due to glue records. We should list registry providers and their effective minimum TTLs in runbook.

deploy-bot: [09:37Z] runbook updated: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dns-failover (edited by anya) :thumbsup:

mike: Good. Keep me updated on error budget burn and if we need to open a billing exception for extra capacity.

anya: Will do. Current plan: maintain 95% shift for next 30m, monitor resolver split and latency. If split persists beyond 30m, we'll move to hostname swap approach and notify account teams.

carla: :thumbsup: I'll post a short note to support with guidance for customers who report they still hit eu-west.

infra-bot: [09:46Z] summary: mitigation in progress — weights changed, additional capacity requested, runbook updated.

mike: Thanks team — postmortem owners assigned, let's regroup after stability confirmed.
